title: Introduce authorization-policy safelist and KMS provenance decorator
author: Amelia Torres
description:
Context: We observed two operational gaps during recent compliance reviews: 1) policy drift where temporary emergency RBAC allowances persisted beyond intended windows, causing noisy audits and manual cleanup; 2) lack of strong provenance metadata in audit records when KMS-wrapped operator credentials were used, which makes forensic reconstruction across multi-region KMS providers difficult. This PR introduces two coordinated pieces: (A) an authorization-policy safelist that lets platform teams declare short-lived, auditable allowlists for specific routes/operators with enforced TTLs and auto-expiry, and (B) a KMS provenance decorator that appends stable provenance metadata (provider, key-alias, wrapping-hash) to audit events and signs it with a dedicated service key so downstream compliance tooling can validate origin and detect cross-region wrapping mismatches.

Motivation: enable safe emergency allowances without long-term policy drift, and give compliance & SRE reliable cryptographic provenance in audit streams for incidents and periodic attestations.

Changes: - Introduced new RBACv2 safelist API surface (yaml policy snippets + runtime enforcement). Safelist entries are declared as: route, operator_set, valid_from, ttl_seconds, justification_id. - Runtime enforcer validates TTL on read; expired entries are rejected and logged as policy violations. - Admin console surface: basic UI form + staged rollout flag. This change is feature-flagged (feature.authz_safelist) and defaults to off. - KMS provenance decorator: middleware that reads KMS usage context when operator-scoped credentials (<operator-kms-token>) were used, constructs a compact provenance JSON, computes a provenance-hash, and attaches a signed envelope to the audit event (audit.provenance_envelope). The decorator supports a primary KMS and a fallback vault for HSM signing in air-gapped installs. - Added a small verification CLI (tools/kms-provenance-verify) used by compliance automation to validate envelope signatures and compare wrapping-hashes across audit windows. - Policy linter updates to warn when a safelist is created without justification_id or without explicit expiry. - Migration: This PR includes a one-time background job that scans existing temporary roles labeled "temp-emergency" and emits reconciliation suggestions as ticketed findings (Linear: ENG-4221).

Tests and validation: - Unit tests for safelist TTL, expiry handling, and linter warnings. - Integration test that simulates operator credential flow across two KMS providers and verifies the provenance envelope is present in the audit payload. - End-to-end smoke test that exercises console create/edit of safelist entry (flagged).

Rollout plan: - Stage 1 (week 0): Merge behind feature flag; run integration tests in canary. - Stage 2 (week 1): Enable feature.flag for internal platform-only orgs; run compliance validation (provenance verification) against historical audit samples. - Stage 3 (week 3): Controlled enablement for customers with dedicated capacity, opt-in.

Monitoring: new metrics added: authz.safelist.created, authz.safelist.expired, audit.provenance.envelope_count, audit.provenance.verify_failures.

Backout plan: disable feature.authz_safelist and rollback the middleware image; provenance decorator can be disabled by config.provenance.enabled=false.

Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked in Linear ENG-4221 - [x] Unit + integration tests - [x] Feature flag gating - [x] Console fields behind staged rollout flag - [x] Migration job emits findings for review - [x] CI green for main + canary Runs: See CI summary below for details. Notes: The signed envelope uses the existing service signing key (rotated monthly) but we included a pluggable signer interface to swap to HSM in private installs. Related work: complements ENG-3952 (policy linter) and SEC-104 (audit retention mapping).

review_conversation: Rajat Menon: Can we ensure the safelist entries are immutable once created and only extendable via a documented approval workflow? Please add a test for attempted post-creation mutation.
Amelia Torres (author): Added DB constraint + API rejects mutations to created_at/created_by/justification_id; added mutation test in integration suite.
Lin Chen: The provenance envelope size looks nontrivial — how will this affect audit ingest costs? Suggest making envelope optional per-org via config.

Amelia Torres (author): Made provenance attach optional via config.provenance.enabled (default true for internal); added metrics to measure envelope size and ingest rate; documented cost considerations in docs.

ci_summary: Initial pipeline flaky test (integration/authz) failed on canary due to setup race; fixed by adding a retry to test harness. Final CI run: all checks passed: unit (pass), linters (pass), integration (pass), e2e (pass).
release_notes: Introduces an RBACv2 safelist to allow short-lived, auditable route/operator allowances with enforced TTLs and an optional KMS provenance envelope attached to audit records for cryptographic origin tracing. Feature gated and disabled by default for public customers.
notes_for_compliance: Envelope format: base64(signed_payload) where signed_payload = HMAC(service_signing_key, provenance_json) currently; provenance_json contains {provider, key_alias, region_hint, wrapping_hash, timestamp}. Compliance automation should call tools/kms-provenance-verify against audit segments. Key distribution: compliance will be provisioned read-only verifier keys via SEC-119.
migration_notes: One-time background job (service/authz/reconcile_temp_roles.go) emits Linear findings and does NOT auto-delete roles. Operators must review suggested reconciliations. Job runs under feature flag and logs to ops.reconciliation.
security_impact_assessment: Risk: increased audit payload size and exposure of limited KMS metadata (non-secret) to audit stream. Mitigations: envelope is signed, provenance excludes raw key material, and provenance attachment is opt-out per org. No plaintext keys are written anywhere. Threats considered: cross-region key mismatch attacks (detectable via wrapping_hash mismatch), replay (timestamp in envelope), and signer compromise (monthly rotation; emergency revoke documented).
